items.work: Thesaurus Linguae Aegyptiae, Original Earlier Egyptian sentences, corpus v18, premium (22 December 2023): 12,773 fully intact sentences from witnesses older than the New Kingdom, each with hieroglyphs (Unicode), transliteration, lemmatization, part of speech, glossing, a German translation and its date range — Hugging Face repository commit a7ba9e9d1a74a9a0f919b024ba84dd6d643b2966; the file's sha256 equals the one the repository publishes for it (13d4f6e1…)
The dataset card of the TLA release (README.md), its statement of scope, curation and licence

Kurt Sethe, Die altaegyptischen Pyramidentexte nach den Papierabdrucken und Photographien des Berliner Museums, Bd. III–IV: Kritischer Apparat; Beschreibung der Inschriften; Konkordanz der Texte; Epigraphik (Leipzig, 1922) — University of Toronto copy

normalization: Files as fetched. Internet Archive OCR text layers as fetched, uncorrected (text/<slug>.ocr.txt); the scan under original/ is the witness. Library of Congress and FAMSI PDFs are image files without a text layer: the page is the only reading. The TLA JSONL is seated as fetched; a reading text is derived from it by code, one sentence per line: hieroglyphs, a tab, the transliteration, a tab, the German translation, a tab, the date range.
scope: Earlier Egyptian in its own script as a machine-readable corpus: the TLA's release holds only sentences fully intact and unambiguously readable (12,773 of 55,026 in its database), with no attribution of each sentence to its text; its date ranges place them from the Old Kingdom to the Second Intermediate Period. The Pyramid Texts are seated in Sethe's apparatus volumes (III–IV); his text volumes (Bd. I, 1908; Bd. II, 1910) were not found in an open scan reachable in this pass: QUEUED. The Coffin Texts (de Buck, 1935–61) are in copyright and are not seated.

why_seated: Seated with the Book of the Dead so that the shelf holds the older language beneath it, in hieroglyphs a machine can read, and the oldest religious corpus in the world, the Pyramid Texts, in the edition that numbered its spells.
ruling: Lee Sharks, 2026-10-23: "detour for an ea-corpora searing. lets see. whats available of mayan texts? and then i dont think we have much or any deteurocanonical second temple lit - all those apocalypses. and what about the ethiopian canon? and euclid. all in original language or as close to it as possible. what else?" — "and the Egyptian book of the dead" — "and what about the fragments of the book of baalim? i might be miswriting this. recent discovery. if theyre available anywhere." — "yes yes yes to all - what a meal."
